summary.text: Adrian Smith is the Republican incumbent seeking an eleventh term representing Nebraska's 3rd District. A Gering native, he worked as an educator and real estate agent, served on the Gering City Council and in the Nebraska Legislature, and was elected to the U.S. House in 2006. He sits on the Ways and Means Committee, where he chairs the Subcommittee on Trade.

paragraphs.text: Smith was born in Scottsbluff, Nebraska, and his House website describes him as a Gering native whose family has lived in Nebraska for six generations.
He attended Liberty University from 1989 to 1990 before earning a B.A. from the University of Nebraska in 1993.
According to his House website, he worked as an educator and a real estate agent before his election to Congress.
Smith served on the Gering City Council from 1994 to 1998 and then in the Nebraska State Senate from 1999 to 2007, representing District 48.
He was elected to the U.S. House in 2006 and has represented Nebraska's 3rd District since 2007.

His House website says Smith has served on the Ways and Means Committee since 2010; in the 2025-2026 term he is chair of its Trade Subcommittee and a member of its Health Subcommittee, and he also serves on the Joint Committee on Taxation.

The site cites his work on trade agreements, including the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement, and on the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, and lists his membership in the Agriculture Trade, Biofuels, Modern Agriculture and Rural caucuses and the House Democracy Partnership.
According to the site, he and his wife, Andrea, live in Gering with their two children.
